name: slice-b-buildings
note: Slice B, the BUILDINGS lane (docs/art-pipeline-plan.md §4b; write-up in docs/art/slice-b/buildings.md). Everything is matched to the approved farmhouse, which is the FIRST style ref in styles/elsinore/style.json, so the prompts point at it as 'the first attached image' instead of attaching it twice. Each subject sends the game's OLD drawing (guides/control-*.png, rendered by guides.js) as the 'redraw this, keep its identity' reference, second to last, and its footprint guide LAST: building2.png (2 x 2 crafting stations, the open-air cut-away template), building3.png (3 x 3 closed shops with a hanging picture sign), tree.png (1 x 1 trees with one full tile of headroom). Two candidates of a subject are two subject keys (dairy-a / dairy-b) rather than --n 2, so both land on the contact sheet. Hard budget for the lane: 14 images.

dairy-a.prompt: SUBJECT: the DAIRY, a crafting station where milk is churned into butter and pressed into cheese. CRAFTING-STATION TEMPLATE, shared by every 2 x 2 crafting station in this game: an open-air, cut-away workshop, NOT a closed house. A back wall of the farmhouse's stone-and-plaster runs along the back (top) edge of the footprint; two short side walls of the same stone come forward from its ends about a third of the way; there is NO front wall and NO roof over the front, so the camera looks straight into the workshop. A narrow strip of the farmhouse's golden thatch with its wooden ridge beam sits along the top of the back wall only, like an awning. The floor inside is packed ochre earth with a few flagstones. On that open floor stands the WORK, drawn big and obvious so a player recognises the station at a glance: for the Dairy, a wooden butter churn with its plunger handle, a big round yellow cheese wheel with a wedge cut out on a low wooden table, and a tin milk pail; four white milk bottles in a wooden crate stand against one side wall. Materials, outline, shading, the lower-right contact shadow and the colours are copied from the farmhouse in the FIRST attached image: this station stands in the same village. The second-to-last attached image is the game's OLD drawing of the Dairy: keep what makes it recognisable (the milk bottles in their crate, a touch of its pale blue on the churn's bands and the table) but do NOT copy its closed-house shape; the template above wins. The LAST attached image is a layout guide, a patch of the board grid with a tan 2 x 2 square: the station fills that 2 x 2 square ENTIRELY and stays inside it, back wall along the square's top edge, ground contact on the square's bottom edge, a soft contact shadow to the lower right. Fill the surrounding squares with plain short grass in the style, no props outside the square, and draw the faint grid lines as thin tile edges. Do not leave the tan square tan.

den-a.prompt: SUBJECT: the WARRIOR'S DEN, a shop that sells weapons and fighting gear. CLOSED-BUILDING TEMPLATE, shared by every 3 x 3 shop in this game: the farmhouse in the FIRST attached image built bigger: the same golden thatch roof with its wooden ridge beam, the same stone chimney, the same stone-and-plaster front wall on a stone foundation course, the same dark wooden door with an iron ring placed in the middle of the front wall, and one shuttered window on each side of the door. Same outline, shading, lower-right contact shadow and colours: this building stands in the same village. SIGN: a square wooden signboard hangs on two short chains from a black iron bracket fixed to the front wall, just above and to the right of the door, facing the camera, with ONE simple flat painted picture on it and NO letters: for the Warrior's Den, two crossed swords. The second-to-last attached image is the game's OLD drawing of the Warrior's Den: keep what makes it recognisable (walls of grey stone with less plaster showing than the farmhouse, the sword sign) but rebuild it on the template above, which wins. The LAST attached image is a layout guide, a patch of the board grid with a tan 3 x 3 square: the building fills that 3 x 3 square ENTIRELY and stays inside it, roof ridge along the square's top edge, ground contact on the square's bottom edge, a soft contact shadow to the lower right. Fill the surrounding squares with plain short grass in the style, no props outside the square, and draw the faint grid lines as thin tile edges. Do not leave the tan square tan.

oak-tree.prompt: SUBJECT: an OAK TREE for the board, a resource the player chops for wood. The second-to-last attached image is the game's OLD drawing of the oak: keep its identity (a round, broad, leafy green crown on a short red-brown trunk) and redraw it in the approved style of the first attached images: a dark outline, the foliage drawn as a few big crisp leaf clusters with a lit upper-left side and a shaded lower-right side, flat fills, a soft contact shadow on the grass to the lower right of the trunk. TREE RULE: a tree stands on one tile and rises one full tile above it, so it is two tiles tall, taller than a person. The LAST attached image is a layout guide, a patch of the board grid with one pale centre tile and a lighter tile directly above it, boxed together by a dashed line: the trunk stands on the pale tile with its base on that tile's bottom edge, the crown rises up through the lighter tile to no higher than the dashed box's top, and the crown may spread a little wider than the box, up to a quarter of a tile on each side, no more. Fill the other squares with plain short grass in the style (no props) and draw the faint grid lines as thin tile edges. Do not leave any guide square pale.
